category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names the mass-capacity mix-up trap with concrete teacher moves, but the trap is not anchored in named research and recovery_moves is a flat list ('Use sorting cards', 'Drill is this about holding or weight?', 'Show containers vs solids') rather than diagnostic-conditioned branches keyed to what the child actually showed.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Sarama & Clements 2009 measurement learning trajectory in expanded_walkthrough.rationale, AND restructure recovery_moves into branches: IF child names mass for any container, contrast a full-vs-empty cup; IF child applies capacity to solids, sort containers vs solids; IF child cannot articulate either, drop back to body gestures (cup-hands vs push-down).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Roo anchors minds_on and consolidation and 'I can' success criteria are present, but Roo lacks a distinctive quotable refrain and consolidation/exit_routine has no memorable chant or sentence frame children carry between lessons — exit_routine is only a generic 'My ___ has ___' frame and 'Roo's Attribute Brag' contains discussion prompts but no chant.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a Roo signature refrain that recurs across all 5 lessons (e.g., 'Roo says — every thing you can MEASURE is a thing you can NAME!') and bake it into consolidation as a class call-and-response chant; surface the refrain in lesson_01.consolidation.exit_routine as the closing chant so children carry it forward to Lessons 2-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Vocabulary is precise and child-friendly and progression names attributes before comparing them — clearly Level 3. But the lesson does not let children invent or refine a strategy and compare strategies, and expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (no Battista, Sarama & Clements, or Empson reference; trap is described in plain terms only).
category_feedback.required_fix: In action.steps add a strategy-comparison move at Station C: ask two pairs to share HOW they decided which attribute to name for an ambiguous object (e.g., a backpack — mass or capacity?), then have the class compare reasoning. Also name the underlying concept in expanded_walkthrough.rationale citing Sarama & Clements 2009 measurement trajectory.

summary: Strong pair overall — alignment, instructional balance (puppets explicitly OPTIONAL with substitution), and lesson-worksheet consistency clear Level 4. Three categories sit at Level 3 with concrete paths to 4: research citation plus branched recovery, a signature Roo chant, and a strategy-comparison move at Station C. Worksheet faithfully mirrors all 3 success criteria across Parts 1-3.
